title: Priority-band preemptor with proportional KV eviction and GPU watermarking
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Continuous batching interleaves requests from multiple tenants and workloads. When long-running high-token streams or large KV-backed contexts consume GPU memory, we violate latency SLOs for latency-sensitive requests. Existing preemptors are either all-or-nothing (force-drop) or coarse-grained and do not account for KV cache fragmentation. Goal: Implement a SLO-aware scheduler that enforces fairness via priority bands and proportional resource reclamation. The system should: 1) assign requests to priority bands (real-time, interactive, background) and compute soft/hard watermarks per GPU; 2) allow proportional KV cache eviction (evict less-recent prefixes based on priority/band credits) rather than indiscriminate KV truncation; 3) allow slice preemption with minimal recomputation by retaining reusable KV segments; 4) provide telemetry exposing per-band latency percentiles, eviction rate, and reclaimed bytes; 5) allow runtime policy tuning (band thresholds, credit refill rate) without restart.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler can preempt slices belonging to lower priority band within 50ms of watermark breach
KV eviction reclaims at least 30% GPU memory under high pressure while preserving median latency for high-priority band
End-to-end P99 latency for interactive band stays within SLO (configured per-cluster) during synthetic overload tests
Dashboard shows per-band memory, eviction events, preemption counts, and a replayable trace to reproduce preemption decision for any request id
Feature rollout gated by canary with automatic fallback to current preemptor on error
design_notes: Priority bands: map request metadata + route config to band (real-time, interactive, background). Each band has credits representing allowed outstanding tokens/bytes.
Preemptor mechanics: when per-GPU soft watermark exceeded, drain background band slices first; if hard watermark reached, preempt interactive slices proportionally to credit deficit.

KV eviction: maintain per-request KV segment metadata (prefix ranges + last-accessed). Eviction is proportional: evict segments from requests in low-priority bands first, but avoid evicting segments younger than configurable TTL to reduce recompute.

GPU watermarking: use mixed metrics - arena allocated bytes + device memory fragmentation estimate from allocator + model KV resident size. Calibrate watermarks per model and sequence-length histogram.
Fairness policy: token-credit bucket that refills at band-level; scheduler prefers fairness-adjusted order over strict FIFO for interactive workloads to prevent starvation of medium-priority clients.
Fallback: policy can be toggled to legacy preemptor via runtime flag; on error we log full decision context and revert per-GPU state to last stable checkpoint.
tasks: Prototype band-aware credit buckets in batcher scheduler loop
Add per-request KV segment registration and last-accessed bookkeeping
Implement proportional eviction algorithm using sampled segment list to limit CPU overhead
Add GPU watermark estimator hook into runtime allocator
Create canary rollout plan and runtime flags
Add telemetry and dashboards for per-band metrics and traces
Write unit + integration tests and synthetic overload benchmark
comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created after post-mortem for incident INC-2026-02 where KV-heavy streaming request caused P99 spikes for interactive routes.

2026-03-11 Liam Chen: Spike prototype shows we can reclaim ~35% of GPU memory by evicting low-priority KV segments; however eviction latency needs bounding — plan to sample segment list to avoid scanning full KV index.

2026-03-11 Design review (Marta Ruiz): Prefer explicit per-request segment metadata to opaque allocator bookkeeping. Ask: how will eviction affect cold-start wins? Suggest TTL floor of 2s for recently-accessed segments.
2026-03-12 Ben Carter (SRE): Add safety: when preempting interactive slices, attempt soft preemption (pause/resume) before hard cancel. Also require audit logs for any hard preemption for compliance.

2026-03-12 Liam Chen: Implemented initial credit-bucket limiter and GPU watermark hooks in local branch. Running synthetic benchmark against models/gpt-3-like to validate P99 for interactive band. Next: integrate KV segment registry and eviction sampler.
